risks.risk: The CPU is not a Core i3, or is a very old generation (e.g., 1st or 2nd gen) which affects performance and value.
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen (e.g., Windows System Properties or BIOS) showing the exact CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic low-end CPU, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The storage is not a 500GB HDD, or it is a slow or failing drive.
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen showing storage details, or a video of the drive being accessed to check for errors or speed.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a smaller or slower drive, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The RAM is not 4GB, or it is a single stick which limits upgradeability.
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen showing RAM details, or a video of the system running memory diagnostics.
risks.if_unproven: priced as less than 4GB or non-upgradable, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The screen has dead pixels, burn-in, or backlight issues not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video of the screen displaying solid colors (white, black, red, green, blue) and moving patterns to check for defects.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially defective screen, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The unit has internal damage, overheating issues, or is not fully functional (e.g., keyboard/mouse not working, ports not working).
risks.proof: A video of the unit being powered on, showing all ports working, keyboard and mouse responding, and system running smoothly.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially non-functional or with hidden faults, which reduces value.
